subsections.poetic_cipher: The circle is memory. The axis is relation. The difference becomes a vector. The vector keeps a phase. The phase becomes a glider. The glider meets its shadow. The shadow finds a third point. And the path becomes a universe.
subsections.cipher_explanation: The cipher compresses the paper's central chain into a sequence of transformations. The circle represents phase and the persistence of relational state. The axis represents the reference relation through which orientation becomes meaningful. A surviving difference can be represented as an oriented vector. That vector carries a phase whose persistence defines the glider. The glider's complementary inverse supplies the dyadic structure. The dyad alone describes opposition but does not necessarily provide closure; the third point introduces contextual relation and permits triadic closure. At cosmological scale, the same relational grammar is proposed as a possible description of differentiation from an initially unresolved state into increasingly structured coherent configurations. The final phrase, 'the path becomes a universe,' is therefore a poetic statement of the paper's central ontological possibility: what appears as a universe may be understood as a coherent trajectory through a relational state space rather than merely as a collection of objects occupying a pre-existing container.
content: The formal development of this paper can be read as a sequence beginning with the smallest possible distinction. Point Space provides a domain in which points can be related, but a point considered in isolation does not yet provide motion, orientation, or identity. These arise through relation.

A relation establishes a difference. When that difference is directional, it may be represented by a vector. When the relational configuration persists through transformation, the vector becomes part of an evolving phase structure. The important object is therefore not the isolated coordinate but the pattern of relations that survives the transition from one state to another.

The circle provides the first compact geometry for this persistence. Phase can change while remaining phase; a configuration may rotate through its state space without losing the relational identity that makes it recognizable. In this sense, the circle is memory rather than merely a clock. It represents the capacity of a structure to remain itself while changing.

When this persistent phase propagates through the coherence field, the resulting structure is identified as a glider. The glider is therefore not introduced as a small particle hidden inside Point Space. It is a pattern whose identity consists in the preservation of relational coherence across transformation. Its motion is the continuation of that pattern through successive configurations.

The glider then encounters its complementary description. The inverse motif is not necessarily a second material object or an independently existing antiparticle. It is the relational complement through which the original motif becomes fully specified as an opposition. The resulting dyad expresses difference as oscillation: each side defines the other, and their relationship supplies a natural phase opposition.

Yet opposition alone does not necessarily constitute closure. A pair can alternate indefinitely without supplying an independent relation that determines why the alternation should stabilize into a persistent structure. The third point therefore enters not as an arbitrary preference for the number three, but as a candidate contextual degree of freedom. The triad can close the relation that the dyad merely opens.

The Bloch sphere provides the geometric extension of this idea. The phase circle is retained, but the state is now situated within a larger geometry in which an observation or reference axis can be selected. What watches becomes the axis: not because an observer creates an otherwise nonexistent state, but because distinguishability requires a relation against which the state can be resolved.

From this perspective, coherence is never simply a property possessed by an isolated configuration. It is coherence relative to a relation, a comparison domain, or an allowed transformation. The same configuration can therefore participate in different descriptions without requiring that one description be metaphysically privileged over all others.

The cosmological extension follows the same grammar. The earliest state is modeled as a limiting condition of maximal unresolved possibility. Cosmogenesis is then represented as differentiation: distinctions become available, coherence gradients emerge, and persistent structures become possible. What is conventionally described as expansion may, within the framework, be interpreted as the relaxation of a coherence structure through which increasingly differentiated configurations become accessible.

The two-universe construction makes the same principle visible at a larger scale. Two complementary coherent structures may oppose one another along an axis, but their opposition alone leaves a residual problem of closure. The third vector supplies the missing relation. The universe is therefore not represented simply as one thing opposed to another; it is represented as a relational structure in which opposition and context jointly determine the stable configuration.
The sequence can consequently be compressed symbolically as follows:

The symbolic progression is not intended as a new physical law. It is a mnemonic representation of the dependencies developed throughout the paper: domain permits distinction; distinction permits orientation; orientation permits phase; persistent phase permits the glider; complementarity produces the dyad; contextual relation permits triadic closure; and the resulting coherent structures provide the conceptual basis for the cosmological application.

The final movement is therefore not from particle to universe, but from relation to structure. The universe appears at the end of the chain because the framework begins by asking what must persist for any structure to be recognizable at all.

In this sense, infinity is not merely an enormous distance or an indefinitely large number of objects. It can arise whenever distinctions remain unresolved and the system continues to generate alternative descriptions. Closure changes the character of that infinity. Equivalence can identify configurations that are observationally indistinguishable, while coherence can constrain which transitions remain accessible. The apparently infinite can therefore possess finite or structured relational form without requiring that the underlying possibility space itself be finite.
The paper thus returns to its beginning: a point, a relation, a difference. Everything that follows is an elaboration of what can happen when that difference survives.

subsections.title: Future Work
objectives: Specify the mathematical, computational, and empirical program required to advance the framework.
Identify the minimum formal results required before the framework can support stronger physical claims.
Separate foundational mathematical questions from model-specific questions and cosmological tests.
Define a staged research program in which each subsequent claim depends on previously established structures.
Identify possible empirical discriminants between coherence-based cosmology and existing cosmological models.
Preserve the distinction between the mathematical framework, its physical interpretation, and the broader Noor Library ontology.
subsections.poetic_cipher: The path beyond the map is not another world; it is the work required to make the map true.
subsections.cipher_explanation: The framework currently provides a connected set of definitions, constructions, models, and hypotheses, but several of its strongest claims remain to be demonstrated. Future work therefore consists not simply of adding more concepts, but of progressively converting conceptual structures into mathematically well-defined objects, deriving their consequences, testing their stability, and determining whether those consequences correspond to observable physical phenomena. The ultimate test is not whether the framework can describe itself coherently, but whether it produces constrained predictions that survive comparison with mathematics, computation, and observation.
content: The present framework should be regarded as the beginning of a research program rather than a completed cosmological theory. Its central constructions—Point Space, relational coherence, the glider, inverse motifs, dyadic oscillation, triadic closure, Bloch-sphere representation, and coherence-gradient cosmogenesis—form a proposed chain of description. The next stage is to determine which links in that chain can be established mathematically, which require additional assumptions, and which produce experimentally or observationally distinguishable consequences.

The first priority is foundational formalization. Point Space must be specified as a mathematical object with an explicit domain, topology or metric structure where required, and a precise definition of the relations permitted between points. Coherence must then be defined as a functional over those relations rather than treated as an intuitive scalar notion. This distinction is essential because the framework's central claim is that coherence is relational: its value depends upon the structure against which a configuration is evaluated.

Once these foundations are established, the proposed coherence field must be examined as a genuine dynamical system. The candidate evolution equation must be shown to be mathematically well-posed under explicitly stated initial and boundary conditions. Stability, existence, uniqueness, regularity, and long-time behavior should be investigated before the field is assigned a physical interpretation.

The next major objective is the glider. A glider should be defined through invariant or approximately invariant relational structure rather than through visual resemblance alone. The research program should identify the mathematical conditions under which a coherence motif can propagate while preserving its identity, determine whether such solutions exist for the proposed field dynamics, and classify their stability. If the glider is to serve as a fundamental model of persistent motion, its persistence must follow from identifiable dynamical conditions rather than from its definition alone.

The inverse motif and dyadic system should then be analyzed independently. In particular, the proposed instability of a purely dyadic configuration should be established rather than assumed. It is possible that some dyadic systems admit stable solutions under particular couplings or boundary conditions. Such cases would not invalidate the triadic construction; instead, they would clarify the precise conditions under which a third relational degree of freedom becomes necessary.

Triadic closure represents the next mathematical target. The framework proposes that a third relational vector can close and stabilize a complementary pair. Future work should therefore derive the conditions for phase locking, identify fixed points and periodic or traveling solutions, and determine the eigenvalue or Lyapunov conditions governing stability. The important question is not merely whether three components can be made stable, but whether triadic closure provides a minimal or otherwise distinguished mechanism for stability.

The Bloch-sphere construction should subsequently be formalized as a geometric representation of relational orientation. Future work should determine exactly which aspects of the circle-to-sphere construction are mathematical identities, which are analogies to quantum-state geometry, and which—if any—are intended as physical claims about quantum systems. The observer axis should likewise be defined as a reference structure within the mathematics without introducing a privileged physical observer.

The cosmological program requires a separate level of validation. The complexity-inversion hypothesis should be translated into a quantitative quantity that can be related to known thermodynamic, informational, or statistical measures. The proposed relationship between coherence relaxation and cosmological expansion must then be derived or explicitly parameterized. A viable cosmological model must reproduce established observations before any claim that it replaces or eliminates existing cosmological mechanisms can be considered.

Finally, the framework should be compared against observational cosmology. Candidate observables include the expansion history H(z), distance-redshift relations, structure growth, early-universe behavior, cosmic background observables, and any predicted deviations from the standard cosmological model. A successful theory must identify not merely a reinterpretation of existing observations but at least one constrained consequence that could in principle distinguish it from competing models.

The broader Library ontology should be investigated only after the mathematical core has been sufficiently formalized. Recursive Bloch geometry, equivalence classes, total adjacency, constrained coherent navigation, and the distinction between mathematical accessibility and physical accessibility provide a larger interpretive framework, but the central results of PHYS-CORE-004 should remain expressible without requiring prior acceptance of that ontology.

The resulting research program is therefore deliberately staged: first establish the mathematical substrate, then establish coherent dynamics, then classify persistent motifs, then analyze dyadic and triadic stability, then formalize observer-relative geometry, and only afterward derive and test cosmological consequences. Each stage should produce explicit objects, equations, simulations, or empirical tests that constrain the next stage.

The ultimate objective is not to make the framework increasingly elaborate, but increasingly falsifiable. If the proposed coherence structures cannot support the required mathematics, the framework must be revised. If they can support the mathematics but produce no distinguishable physical consequences, their status should remain that of a useful mathematical or conceptual model. If they generate novel quantitative predictions that survive comparison with observation, then the framework may provide grounds for a stronger physical interpretation.

open_questions: What precise mathematical structure should Point Space possess?
Is Point Space best represented as a metric space, graph, manifold, discrete complex, or another structure?
What is the correct domain of the coherence functional?
Is coherence fundamentally scalar, vectorial, tensorial, or relationally higher-order?
Can the candidate coherence dynamics be derived from a variational, informational, geometric, or other foundational principle?
Under what conditions is the coherence evolution equation well-posed?
What conserved quantities or Lyapunov functions exist?
Do stable glider solutions exist?
What invariants define glider identity?
Can gliders be classified into distinct families?
Does the glider velocity follow from the coherence gradient, and if so, what is the exact relation?
Is dyadic instability mathematically necessary, or are stable dyadic regimes possible?
Is triadic closure necessary, sufficient, or merely one mechanism of stabilization?
Can triadic stability conditions be derived analytically?
Can the phase-locking condition be obtained from an explicit coupling Hamiltonian or dynamical system?
What is the precise physical meaning, if any, of the third vector?
What aspects of the Bloch-sphere construction are mathematical representation and what aspects are intended as physical claims?
Can observer-relative orientation be formalized without introducing a privileged observer?
Can symbolic complexity be related quantitatively to an established information-theoretic or thermodynamic quantity?
Can the cosmological coherence variable be defined independently of the desired cosmological result?
Can cosmological expansion be derived from coherence relaxation rather than imposed as an ansatz?
Does the framework reproduce the observed expansion history?
Does it reproduce early-universe constraints and structure formation?
Does it predict any measurable deviation from ΛCDM?
Can the two-universe interference model be interpreted as a mathematical toy model without requiring literal multiple universes?
Can the equivalence-class interpretation of infinity yield a useful formal reduction of apparently infinite configuration spaces?
How does mathematical accessibility differ from physical accessibility in a formal dynamical model?
Can the recursive Bloch and Library constructions be recovered as a mathematical extension of the ontology-free core?
limitations: The present framework does not yet provide a complete derivation from fundamental physical principles.
Several central quantities, including the coherence functional and cosmological coherence variable, remain insufficiently specified for quantitative use.
The candidate coherence-field dynamics require formal well-posedness and stability analysis.
The existence of glider solutions has not yet been established for a fully specified physical dynamical system.
The claim that dyadic systems are intrinsically unstable remains a hypothesis until counterexamples and stability conditions are systematically analyzed.
Triadic closure has not yet been shown to be mathematically minimal or universally necessary.
The Bloch-sphere construction establishes a useful geometric representation but does not by itself establish a new physical interpretation of quantum mechanics.
The complexity-inversion interpretation of cosmogenesis remains speculative until a quantitative complexity measure and dynamical correspondence are provided.
The proposed coherence-based interpretation of cosmological expansion requires comparison with established cosmological observables.
Internal coherence of the Noor corpus is not independent empirical validation.
The Library ontology is deliberately not required for the mathematical core and should not be used as evidence for the physical claims.
A successful mathematical model would not automatically establish that its structures correspond to physical reality.

subsections.handoff: The framework therefore ends not at a final cosmological claim but at a research boundary: Point Space must become mathematics, coherence must become a defined functional, gliders must become demonstrable solutions, triadic closure must become a stability result, and cosmogenesis must become a quantitatively testable model. Only then can the path from relational motif to physical cosmology be judged by the same standard imposed on any other physical theory.

subsections.title: Appendix A — Definitions and Notation
objectives: Provide a canonical vocabulary for PHYS-CORE-004.
Separate conceptual definitions from candidate mathematical definitions.
Provide stable notation for independent generation of paper sections.
Prevent later sections from silently changing the meaning of core terms.
subsections.poetic_cipher: Name the stone before building the cathedral.
subsections.cipher_explanation: The paper depends upon several terms whose ordinary meanings can differ substantially from their meanings within the proposed framework. This appendix establishes the local vocabulary before those terms are used in mathematical or cosmological arguments.

The total domain containing all states, including coherent and incoherent states.
Indistinguishability under a chosen comparison relation.
The domain, subset, or relational context relative to which states are compared for identity, difference, or coherence.
The relation or reference structure against which the coherence or distinguishability of a state is evaluated.
A relational distinction between states under a specified comparison relation.
An oriented relational difference encoding a direction of change between distinguishable states.
A relational measure of compatibility, persistence, or structural consistency relative to a comparison domain and reference relation.
A candidate dynamical field representing the local distribution of coherence over a spatial and temporal domain.
A measure of distinguishability or change between coherence configurations.
A cyclic relational coordinate representing the state or orientation of a persistent motif within a periodic structure.
A persistent relational pattern whose phase or structure survives evolution up to an allowed translation or transformation.
A complementary relational mode associated with a glider through an inverse or opposing transformation.
A relational pair consisting of complementary coherence structures.
A relational structure in which a state, its complementary state, and a contextual reference form a closed dynamical configuration.

The preservation of a motif's defining relational structure under an allowed class of transformations.

epistemic_status_key.formal_concept: A concept whose mathematical meaning can be stated independently of the proposed physical interpretation.
epistemic_status_key.proposed_definition: A definition specific to the ontology developed by this paper.

subsections.scope_note: The definitions in this appendix establish vocabulary rather than proving the claims associated with those terms. In particular, defining a glider does not establish that gliders exist as solutions of a specified dynamical system; defining structural eternity does not establish eternal physical existence; and defining coherence does not establish that coherence is a fundamental physical field.
subsections.handoff: With the vocabulary fixed, the mathematical appendix can state the candidate equations and constructions without repeatedly redefining their terms.

subsections.title: Appendix B — Mathematical Register
subsections.description: Formal mathematical register for PHYS-CORE-004, 'To Infinity, and Beyond'. This appendix collects the mathematical expressions used or proposed throughout the paper, together with their epistemic status, role, dependencies, and interpretation. It is intended as a reference layer rather than a substitute for derivations in the main text.
subsections.title: Mathematical Register
objectives: Collect the mathematical expressions introduced throughout PHYS-CORE-004.
Distinguish definitions, identities, candidate structures, ansätze, hypotheses, and phenomenological models.
Provide a compact mathematical reference for independently generated sections.
Preserve the dependency structure between the mathematical constructions.
Prevent speculative mathematical relations from being mistaken for established physical laws.
subsections.poetic_cipher: The symbols are stones along the path; their arrangement tells us where the path may lead.
subsections.cipher_explanation: The equations in this appendix are not all equivalent in epistemic status. Some define terms, some encode established mathematical identities, and others are proposed structures that require derivation, analysis, simulation, or empirical testing. The register preserves those distinctions so that the mathematical vocabulary of the paper remains coherent without overstating its conclusions.
content: This appendix provides the mathematical register for PHYS-CORE-004.

The expressions are ordered approximately according to the conceptual descent of the paper: total domain, equivalence, relational difference, coherence, field dynamics, glider structure, complementary motifs, triadic resonance, geometric observation, and cosmological application.

An expression marked as a definition specifies terminology used by the paper. An identity records a mathematical relation that follows from the adopted representation. A candidate structure is a proposed formalization whose suitability remains to be established. An ansatz is a proposed form inserted into a model for investigation. A hypothesis is a physical or ontological claim requiring support beyond notation alone.
No expression in this appendix should be interpreted as empirically established merely because it appears in mathematical form.

definitions.definition: The proposed total domain containing all states under consideration, including coherent and incoherent states.
An equivalence relation identifying states that are indistinguishable under a specified comparison relation.
The space of equivalence classes induced by the chosen indistinguishability relation.
A proposed measure or functional describing compatibility, persistence, or structural agreement relative to a comparison domain and reference relation.
A proposed measure of distinguishability between two coherence configurations or relational states.
A candidate scalar field representing local coherence structure over space and time.
A persistent relational pattern whose structure or phase survives evolution up to an allowed transformation or translation.
A complementary coherence configuration related to a glider by an inverse or opposing relational transformation.
A cyclic relational coordinate used to represent the state or orientation of a persistent motif.
A proposed three-component relational condition in which the frequencies and phases of three coupled motifs satisfy a resonance or phase-locking relationship.
A reference direction relative to which a state represented on the Bloch sphere is projected.
The cosmological scale factor used in the standard definition of the Hubble parameter.
The logarithmic time derivative of the cosmological scale factor.

math.label: Library
math.interpretation: The Library is treated as containing coherent and incoherent configurations rather than only physically realized or coherent states.
math.caveat: This is an ontological/conceptual definition, not a standard mathematical specification of a particular set.

math.label: Equivalence
math.role: Represents indistinguishability under a chosen comparison relation.
math.interpretation: Two states are treated as equivalent when the relevant observational or relational structure cannot distinguish them.
math.caveat: The exact equivalence relation must be specified before a rigorous quotient construction can be claimed.

math.label: Quotient
math.role: Represents the space of distinguishability classes.
math.interpretation: Multiple underlying representations may correspond to one relationally distinguishable state.
math.caveat: The mathematical properties of the quotient depend on the structure assigned to L and the properties of ~.

math.label: Relational Coherence
math.role: Defines coherence relative to a comparison domain D and reference relation R.
math.interpretation: Coherence is not necessarily an intrinsic scalar property of x; it may depend on what x is being compared against and how the comparison is constructed.
math.caveat: A complete theory requires a precise definition of D, R, the codomain of C, and its normalization.

math.label: Coherence Difference
math.role: Provides a simple candidate measure of separation between coherence configurations.
math.interpretation: Nonzero difference supplies the minimal mathematical representation of distinguishability.
math.caveat: The norm and representation space must be specified. The expression should not be assumed to be the unique or physically correct coherence difference.

math.label: Candidate Coherence Field
math.expression: \partial_t C = D\nabla^2 C + \lambda C(1-C^2) + \kappa F(\Phi,\nabla C)
math.role: Provides a candidate dynamical environment for coherence structures.
math.interpretation: The terms represent diffusion/spatial smoothing, nonlinear self-organization or saturation, and additional phase/coherence coupling.
math.caveat: This equation is a proposed phenomenological model. Its physical interpretation, dimensional consistency, well-posedness, and solution structure require separate analysis.

math.label: Traveling Glider
math.role: Represents a persistent coherence structure translating with velocity v.
math.interpretation: The glider is identified with a profile whose internal structure remains recognizable while its location changes.
math.caveat: The existence and stability of such solutions must be demonstrated for the selected coherence dynamics.

math.label: Traveling-Wave Reduction
math.role: Reduces the candidate field equation under the traveling-wave ansatz.
math.interpretation: The PDE becomes an ordinary differential equation for the persistent profile F.
math.caveat: The omitted terms must be explicitly derived from the complete field equation before this can function as a rigorous reduction.

math.label: Static Limit
math.role: Connects vanishing relational change with vanishing phase evolution.
math.interpretation: The static limit corresponds to loss of distinguishable phase progression.
math.caveat: The implication requires a dynamical relation between coherence difference and phase velocity; it is not a mathematical consequence of B.5 alone.

math.label: Inverse Relation
math.role: Defines the glider and complementary inverse motif as a dyadic pair.
math.interpretation: The inverse motif represents an opposing or complementary relational mode.
math.caveat: The inverse must not automatically be identified with a physical antiparticle, negative energy, antimatter, or time reversal without an explicit derivation.

math.label: Triadic Resonance
math.role: Represents a generic three-frequency resonance condition.
math.interpretation: The third mode may become dynamically coupled to the two complementary modes when their frequencies satisfy a resonance relation.
math.caveat: The appropriate resonance relation depends on the actual coupling equations and symmetry of the system.

math.label: Triadic Phase Locking
math.role: Represents phase alignment among three coupled motifs.
math.interpretation: A bounded or slowly varying phase difference is proposed as a possible mechanism for persistent triadic coherence.
math.caveat: The stability of phase locking must be demonstrated dynamically.

math.label: Bloch Projection
math.role: Represents projection onto one of two complementary outcomes along an observation axis.
math.interpretation: The observed representation depends on the relative orientation between the state vector and reference axis.
math.caveat: The expression is standard Bloch-sphere geometry when r and n are appropriately normalized.

math.label: Complementary Bloch Projection
math.role: Provides the complementary projection to B.13.
math.interpretation: The pair partitions the two-outcome projection under the selected axis.
math.caveat: The probabilities sum to unity when the standard Bloch representation and normalization conditions hold.

math.label: Hubble Relation
math.role: Defines the Hubble parameter in terms of the cosmological scale factor.
math.interpretation: Provides the standard cosmological quantity against which any coherence-based expansion model must ultimately be compared.
math.caveat: This equation is standard cosmological notation and does not itself imply the coherence interpretation.

math.label: Coherence Expansion Ansatz
math.role: Proposes a relationship between effective cosmic expansion and coherence-field evolution.
math.interpretation: Cosmological expansion may emerge as a macroscopic manifestation of coherence relaxation or reorganization.
math.caveat: This relation is speculative and requires dimensional analysis, derivation from the field dynamics, and comparison with observational cosmology.

subsections.title: Appendix C — Epistemic Status and Claim Classification
subsections.description: Epistemic classification of the principal concepts, mathematical constructions, hypotheses, and interpretations used in PHYS-CORE-004: To Infinity, and Beyond.
subsections.title: Epistemic Status and Claim Classification
objectives: Provide a transparent classification of the claims made throughout PHYS-CORE-004.
Distinguish definitions from mathematical constructions, hypotheses, and interpretations.
Prevent speculative cosmological interpretations from being mistaken for established mathematical consequences.
Provide a consistent epistemic vocabulary for independently generated sections of the paper.
Allow future revisions to promote or demote individual claims as mathematical or empirical work progresses.
subsections.poetic_cipher: Name the stone before building the cathedral.
subsections.cipher_explanation: Every component of the framework must be identified according to what kind of knowledge claim it represents. A definition establishes terminology; a mathematical construction establishes a formal object; a hypothesis proposes a relationship requiring investigation; an interpretation gives meaning to a formal structure without itself constituting proof.
subsections.epistemic_rule: No item classified as a hypothesis or interpretation may be presented as a mathematical consequence unless an explicit derivation establishes that consequence.

definitions.description: Terms introduced to establish the vocabulary and ontology used by the framework. Definitions are stipulated for the purposes of the model and are not empirical claims.

items.name: Relational Coherence Functional
items.description: A proposed functional assigning coherence to a state relative to a comparison domain D and reference relation R.
required_work: Determine whether coherence is scalar, vectorial, tensorial, or higher-order.

items.name: Coherence Difference
items.description: A proposed measure of distinguishability between coherence configurations.
required_work: Define the underlying metric or norm.
Determine whether the quantity is coordinate invariant.
Determine its physical or informational dimensions.

items.name: Coherence-Field PDE
items.description: A candidate dynamical field equation intended to support coherence gradients, relaxation, and persistent structures.
items.candidate_expression: \partial_t C = D\nabla^2 C + \lambda C(1-C^2) + \kappa F(\Phi,\nabla C)

items.name: Traveling-Wave Glider
items.description: A proposed representation of a glider as a coherent traveling-wave structure.
required_work: Determine whether solutions preserve motif identity.

items.name: Velocity/Coherence-Gradient Relation
items.description: A proposed relationship between oriented motion and the local coherence gradient.
required_work: Specify whether the relation is proportional, functional, or merely qualitative.
Derive from the underlying dynamics if possible.

items.name: Triadic Stability Equations
items.description: A coupled three-component coherence system intended to test whether triadic closure can stabilize complementary structures.
required_work: Compare stability against the corresponding dyadic system.

hypotheses.description: Proposed physical or cosmological claims that go beyond the definitions and mathematical constructions of the framework and therefore require derivation, simulation, comparison with existing theory, or empirical evidence.

items.name: Dyadic Instability
items.description: A complementary pair may be unable to maintain a stable nontrivial configuration without an additional contextual degree of freedom.
items.test: Compare the stability spectrum and persistent solutions of dyadic and triadic systems.

items.name: Triadic Stabilization
items.description: A third contextual coherence mode may stabilize a complementary dyad through phase locking or resonance.
items.test: Derive and simulate the coupled triadic dynamics.

items.name: Complexity Inversion
items.description: Cosmogenesis may be understood as a transition from highly unresolved symbolic/coherence complexity toward progressively differentiated states.
items.test: Construct a quantitative complexity measure and compare its predicted evolution with cosmological behavior.

items.name: Early-Universe Unresolved State
items.description: The early universe may correspond to a regime in which distinctions that later become observationally meaningful are highly compressed or unresolved.
items.test: Determine whether the proposed state can reproduce known early-universe observables.

items.name: Coherence-Relaxation Cosmology
items.description: Effective cosmic expansion may emerge from relaxation of a global coherence field rather than requiring expansion to be interpreted as primitive geometric motion.
items.test: Derive an effective scale factor and compare H(z), distance relations, and structure growth against standard cosmology.

items.name: Two-Branch Cosmological Interpretation
items.description: Opposing coherence branches may admit an interpretation as complementary cosmological sectors or universes stabilized through a shared third relational degree of freedom.
items.test: Determine whether the two-branch model has mathematical necessity or whether the cosmological interpretation remains optional.

interpretations.description: Conceptual interpretations of mathematical structures. Interpretations can guide physical intuition but do not constitute independent mathematical or empirical evidence.

items.name: Observer as Relational Axis
items.description: The observer can be represented geometrically as a reference axis relative to which a state is projected or distinguished.

items.name: Phase as Memory
items.description: Cyclic phase can be interpreted as retained relational information about the position of a persistent motif within its evolution.

items.name: Glider as Persistence
items.description: The glider represents existence through persistence of relational structure rather than persistence of a material object at a fixed coordinate.

items.name: Time as Ordered Distinguishability
items.description: Temporal order can be interpreted as the ordering of distinguishable relational states along a coherent trajectory.

items.name: Library as Totality
items.description: The Library can be interpreted as the complete relational domain from which observed coherent trajectories are selected or traversed.

claim_status_rules.rule: A definition establishes terminology or formal convention. It is neither proved nor disproved by empirical observation, although it may be useful or useless.
An identity follows from an established mathematical structure and should be demonstrated or cited.
A proposed mathematical construction whose validity, usefulness, or consequences remain under investigation.
A deliberately simplified mathematical representation intended to test a mechanism.
A substantive claim about physical, cosmological, or ontological behavior that requires support beyond definition.
A conceptual reading of a formal result that provides meaning or intuition but is not itself proof.
A result supported by explicit derivation, mathematical proof, validated computation, or appropriate empirical evidence.

generation_constraints: Generated sections must preserve the epistemic status assigned here.
A hypothesis may not be rewritten as a fact merely for rhetorical smoothness.
A candidate equation must not be described as a governing physical law until its derivation and empirical status justify that language.
Poetic ciphers may guide interpretation but must never be used as mathematical evidence.
Interpretations should be explicitly labeled when they move beyond the mathematical construction.
If subsequent analysis establishes a stronger result, the epistemic status may be promoted with justification.
If subsequent analysis invalidates a proposed result, its status must be demoted or removed rather than silently preserved.

revision_protocol.purpose: Maintain epistemic integrity as the paper develops.
required_for_promotion: or clearly identified logical consequence of previously established premises

subsections.handoff: The paper's equations tell us what can be constructed; its hypotheses tell us what must be tested; its interpretations tell us how the geometry may be understood. Keeping these layers distinct allows the framework to descend further without confusing resonance with proof.
